blinding_compliance: I reviewed only the provided blind packet and general statistical knowledge; I did not access repository internals, hidden truth files, scoring code, other reviewer outputs, paper drafts, or reviews; I did not search the benchmark/paper name on the web.
ai_assistance: AI assistant used to parse the packet and draft this review; no external computation or browsing was performed.

forbidden_at_checkpoint: Concluding that the 60-joint baseline is a single stable process or reporting overall capability indices (Pp/Ppk) as valid process capability without conditioning on the detected level shift.
Interpreting the baseline temporal shift or before/after association as evidence that a specific named line setting or the operational change caused the shift.
Adopting the factorial corner (high chain speed, low rail angle, low air pressure) as an optimized production setting without a confirmatory controlled trial.
Treating the after-window Johnson-SU capability indices as definitive given n=30 and rejected normal fit.
permitted_at_checkpoint: Characterizing the baseline as nonstationary/level-shifted using phase-specific charts, CUSUM, and order regression.
Reporting descriptive baseline statistics and capability indicators with explicit caveats about instability/nonnormality.
Proceeding to the designed factorial analysis to identify controlled factor effects.
Proceeding to a before/after comparison as associational only, with the change identity expressly marked unavailable.
Running distributional sensitivity analyses for capability provided they are labeled non-definitive.
reviews.extra_computation_detail: The baseline phase/CUSUM analysis is a valid nonstationarity route. The downstream factorial DOE is a valid controlled-factor analysis. The before/after comparison is valid for association only, accompanied by a rank sensitivity test and unequal-variance check. After-window capability is appropriately presented as non-definitive sensitivity (Johnson SU) after Shapiro-Wilk rejection; Box-Cox was computed but correctly excluded as implausible.
allowed_alternatives: Phase-based I-MR charting and CUSUM instead of a single overall I-MR chart for a shifted baseline.
Factorial DOE with replication and full-model F-test for designed factor effects, with candidate settings treated as confirmation candidates only.
Before/after Welch t-test or rank test as association-only evidence when the change identity is missing.
Nonnormal capability sensitivity using Johnson SU or other fitted quantile models, explicitly not confirmed with n=30.
evidence: Reported baseline mean 7.263783 mm vs target 7.15 mm; one-sample p=1.1126e-7.
Reported baseline first-half mean 7.1394 mm, second-half mean 7.388167 mm, difference 0.248767 mm, p=1.56e-18; CUSUM first flag at index 22; separate phase I-MR charts show no within-half signals.
Reported DOE full factorial p=0.000239552, R2=94.176%; chain-speed coefficient p=2.94896e-5; rail-angle p=4.61398e-4; chain-speed*rail-angle p=0.002580.
Reported before/after mean increase 0.092367 mm, 95% CI 0.035839-0.148894, p=0.001933; Mann-Whitney p=0.001721; change identity refused.
Reported after-window Shapiro-Wilk p=0.008420; Johnson SU KS p=0.385697, Pp=0.992189, Ppk=0.840650; report states this is not a definitive capability claim.
reviews.rationale: The baseline evidence robustly supports a real level shift rather than a stable baseline: large order effect, half-to-half mean difference, CUSUM signal, and absence of within-phase control-chart signals. The report correctly withholds stable-process capability, correctly stops causal identification of the operational change, and handles downstream DOE/capability analyses as preliminary or sensitivity results. Thus the focal baseline stability advancement should proceed.
reviews.numerical_check: Self-report-only for raw data; spot-checked aggregate arithmetic including baseline half difference 7.388167-7.1394=0.248767 and before/after mean difference 7.284033-7.191667=0.092367, with CI 0.035839-0.148894 spanning the reported difference.
reviews.evidence_problem: Route declaration for factor_significance_gate reports observed p=0.019762 with sampleSize=48, which appears to be from the logged-variable model rather than the 16-run designed factorial; not material because the factorial analysis independently supplies lower p-values for chain speed, rail angle, and interaction.
